description: Workbench-reviewed motive/agency weak-mapping contrast seed batch. Targets agenda, coordination, collusion, court filing allegation, anonymous source, confidence inflation, challenge, contradiction, and conspiracy-label pressure.

entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: They coordinated the talking points.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence asserts coordination pressure and requires direct-link or strong structured-pattern evidence.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: A reference operator is legitimate only after the actor or target has been resolved.
Coordination is legitimate only with direct link evidence or a strong structured pattern that defeats independent-convergence explanations.

evidence_burden: Separate actor class from specific actor.
Check whether the claim changes after reference resolution.
Look for communication records, timing, common source, or control channel.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: require direct-link or strong structured-pattern evidence for coordination
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: not source-driven unless sources are later attached
questions: What direct-link or structured-pattern evidence supports coordination?

entries.text: The media pushed that agenda on purpose.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The media pushed that agenda on purpose.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence attributes agenda or motive pressure and requires actor, goal, mechanism, and evidence.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Agenda framing is legitimate only when the goal, actor, mechanism, and evidence pattern are specified.

evidence_burden: Show documents, incentives, repeated behavior, or admissions.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: bound agenda language by actor, goal, mechanism, and evidence
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: not source-driven unless sources are later attached
questions: Who has the alleged agenda, what is the goal, and what evidence supports that motive claim?

entries.text: The companies colluded to suppress the story.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The companies colluded to suppress the story.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence asserts collusion or coordinated action; this requires direct-link evidence rather than mere similarity.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Collusion is legitimate only with direct-link evidence such as agreement, communication, shared control, or coordinated action that defeats independent convergence.

evidence_burden: Look for agreement, communication records, common control, or shared planning evidence.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: treat collusion as direct-link agency pressure; require agreement, communication, common control, or shared planning evidence
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: not source-driven unless sources are later attached
questions: What agreement, communication, common-control, or shared-planning evidence supports collusion?

entries.text: The court filing alleges coordination between the groups.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The court filing alleges coordination between the groups.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence uses an official filing to preserve an allegation, not an adjudicated finding.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Coordination is legitimate only with direct link evidence or a strong structured pattern that defeats independent-convergence explanations.
A court filing is an official record of allegations or filings; it is not proof of the allegations by itself.
Alleges language is legitimate when it preserves the non-final status of a claim until evidence or adjudication changes it.

evidence_burden: Look for communication records, timing, common source, or control channel.
Separate filed allegation from adjudicated finding.
Inspect exhibits, sworn statements, and court findings separately.
Check whether a finding, admission, or direct evidence exists.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: separate filed allegation from adjudicated finding and inspect attached evidence
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: treat source/status/provenance labels as metadata or prior pressure, not truth
questions: What direct-link or structured-pattern evidence supports coordination?
What exactly does the court filing allege, and what exhibits or findings support it?
Is this only an allegation, or is there adjudication, admission, or direct evidence?

entries.text: An anonymous account leaked the document.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: An anonymous account leaked the document.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence uses a low-trust or anonymous source while preserving inspectable evidence as possible evidence.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Anonymous source status lowers trust prior but does not automatically falsify inspectable evidence.

evidence_burden: Separate source trust from evidence content.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: separate low source trust from the inspectability of the leaked evidence
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: treat source/status/provenance labels as metadata or prior pressure, not truth
questions: Can the leaked document be authenticated independently of the anonymous source?

entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: Someone clearly pressured the witness.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence combines confidence inflation with an agency/pressure claim that needs actor, target, mechanism, and evidence.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Clearly language is legitimate only as rhetoric after the evidence is inspectable; it cannot replace evidence.
Someone is legitimate only as an unresolved actor placeholder until the actor is identified.
Pressure/coercion language is legitimate only when the actor, target, mechanism, and evidence of pressure are identified.

evidence_burden: Check whether evidence supports the claim without the modifier.
Separate unknown actor from known institution.
Check whether the claim depends on actor identity.
Inspect direct evidence such as messages, threats, incentives, or testimony.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: strip confidence inflation and evaluate the underlying claim
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: not source-driven unless sources are later attached
questions: What remains if the confidence word clearly is removed?
Who pressured whom, by what mechanism, and what direct evidence shows it?

entries.text: The claim was challenged by the audit record.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The claim was challenged by the audit record.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence says the claim is being questioned or contested; this creates challenge pressure, not refutation or falsity.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: A challenge is legitimate as pressure against certainty, but it is not the same as refutation or contradiction.

evidence_burden: Identify what part of the claim is challenged.
Identify the reason or evidence for the challenge.
Check whether the challenge weakens, contradicts, or merely questions the claim.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: treat challenge as challenge pressure only; do not convert it into refutation or falsity
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: not source-driven unless sources are later attached
questions: What part of the claim is challenged, and does the challenge weaken, contradict, or merely question it?

entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The transcript contradicted the claim.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence claims an inspectable record conflicts with the claim; contradiction depends on matching definitions, date, and scope.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Transcript evidence is legitimate only when authentic, complete enough for the claim, and mapped to the exact statement.
A record legitimately contradicts a claim only when both cannot be true under the same definitions, date, and scope.

evidence_burden: Map exact quote or absence claim.
Check definitions, timing, and possible reconciliation.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: map the record-to-claim contradiction and check scope before resolution
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: inspect the evidence object directly before support/contradiction movement
questions: What record contradicts the claim, and do the record and claim share the same definitions, date, and scope?

entries.text: Only conspiracy theorists still question the official version.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: Only conspiracy theorists still question the official version.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence applies a stigma/dismissal label that must not replace evidence analysis.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: A challenge is legitimate as pressure against certainty, but it is not the same as refutation or contradiction.
Conspiracy labeling is legitimate only when it distinguishes unsupported coordination claims from evidence-backed coordination claims; otherwise it operates as stigma and dismissal pressure.

evidence_burden: Identify what part of the claim is challenged.
Identify the reason or evidence for the challenge.
Check whether the challenge weakens, contradicts, or merely questions the claim.
Check whether the label addresses evidence or only stigmatizes the claimant.
Separate unsupported theory from inspectable coordination evidence.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: separate stigma/dismissal pressure from evidence analysis
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: not source-driven unless sources are later attached
questions: Does the conspiracy label address evidence, or only stigmatize the claimant?
What part of the claim is challenged, and does the challenge weaken, contradict, or merely question it?
